10.1002_advs.77565: The growing demand for energy storage systems (ESS) driven by the expansion of renewable energy calls for aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries that offer both safety and cost competitiveness. However, the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and Zn anode corrosion, combined with iodine dissolution and polyiodide shuttling at the I 2 cathode, form a degradation loop through interelectrode interactions, that impairs battery lifespan and efficiency. This study proposes a dual‐interface regulation strategy by introducing the multidentate chelator TPEN as an electrolyte additive. This strategy promotes the formation of Zn 2+ –TPEN coordination species (TCC) in the electrolyte, which reconfigures the electric double layer of Zn anode into an interfacial environment with reduced water accessibility via interfacial adsorption, suppressing HER and corrosion, and stabilizing local pH fluctuations while promoting uniform nucleation and deposition. Simultaneously, at the I 2 cathode, it traps polyiodide to reduce free polyiodide concentration and directs the reaction pathway toward the interface, thereby decreasing shuttling and self‐discharge while improving I 2 deposition uniformity. As a result, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell operated stably for over 2000 h and achieved a Coulombic efficiency of over 96.2% and a capacity retention of 92.5% after 200 cycles under high‐loading I 2 (5.5 mAh cm −2 ) and 0.18 C conditions.
10.1002_anie.202510252: Controlling the growth orientation of zinc (Zn) is an effective method of stabilizing Zn anodes. Although Zn (100) exhibits faster Zn electroplating/stripping kinetics than Zn (002), its high chemical reactivity results in susceptibility to water‐induced side reactions. Herein, a two‐pronged electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed to enhance the reversibility of Zn anodes, that is, modulating vertically oriented Zn (100) plating while simultaneously constructing a water‐poor electrical double layer (EDL). Mechanistic studies revealed that the difluoro(oxalato)borate (DFOB − ) anions of sodium‐difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) function as a Zn 2+ trapping agent at the inner Helmholtz layer, displacing active water molecules and inducing the preferential deposition of Zn on the Zn (100) crystal facets, thus effectively inhibiting both side reactions and dendrite growth. Consequently, a symmetrical cell with the ZnSO 4 /NaDFOB electrolyte exhibited a long lifetime of over 950 h under severe conditions of 10 mA cm −2 and 5 mAh cm −2 . Furthermore, a practical Zn||NH 4 V 4 O 10 pouch cell could achieves a high capacity of 156 mAh at industrial‐level mass loading of 16.6 mg cm −2 . This work provides insights for achieving stable Zn anodes via electrolyte engineering‐triggered crystallographic orientation and EDL regulation.
10.1002_cjoc.70710: Comprehensive Summary Electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 – ) reduction to ammonia (NO 3 RR) attracts attention for its mild conditions and ability to convert NO 3 – pollutants into valuable ammonia, yet achieving high yield and long‐term stability at low overpotentials remains a major challenge. Here, a homemade carbon paper (HCP) catalyst support with high specific surface area, excellent conductivity, and robust structural stability was constructed from carbon nanotubes (CNTs). Leveraging the uniform surface properties and high surface energy of carbon nanotubes, active CuNi metals self‐assemble to form a uniform, dense coating structure with a shell thickness of approximately 3 nm. This structure maximizes active‐site exposure and facilitates rapid, spatially coupled tandem reactions during NO 3 RR within the same interfacial region, thereby boosting overall catalytic performance, while the intrinsically high surface energy of CNTs thermodynamically suppresses Ostwald ripening of the metal components, conferring excellent long‐term catalytic stability. Meanwhile, efficient electrocatalytic NO 3 RR at low potentials was achieved by tuning NO 3 – adsorption via Cu and promoting the hydrogenation process through Ni. As a result, the CuNi/HCP catalyst delivered an NH 3 production rate of 16.73 mg·h –1 ·cm –2 at –0.08 V vs. RHE (~90% FE), increasing to 27.15 mg·h –1 ·cm –2 and 96.85% FE at –0.28 V, with stable operation over 456 h.
10.1016_j.energy.2025.135892: As the share of volatile renewable energy sources in the electrical power grid continues to grow, needed additional system flexibility can be provided by energy storages, power transmission, and demand-side-management. The interplay between these three elements has recently gained interest in the field of energy system modeling. This study aims to determine the impact of potential non-industrial demand-side-management technologies, including heat pumps, controlled charging of battery electric vehicles, refrigeration, and air conditioning, on energy costs and battery storage requirements in Germany's future electrical power system. The model is analyzed using a novel modeling approach that enables a comparison of flexible loads responding to different market conditions: centralized market conditions with uniform market prices and decentralized market conditions with nodal prices, considering the congestion management potential of demand-side-management. The results show that non-industrial flexible loads can significantly affect the need for battery storage if high residual load peaks can be reduced by the specific technology. However, energy costs may only be reduced by up to 10 %. The study emphasizes the potential of demand-side-management for mitigating grid congestions, demonstrating that investment in battery storages may be lowered by up to 40 % when comparing centralized and decentralized market conditions. • Analysis of four non-industrial DSM technologies in national energy system model. • Modelling method compares DSM response to uniform vs. nodal electricity prices. • DSM may reduce operational energy costs and investment in battery storages. • Grid congestion may limit the cost reduction impact of DSM for electricity market. • Nodal pricing for DSM may support grid management and reduce grid congestion costs.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123481: High-voltage vanadium-based NASICON cathodes for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are fundamentally constrained by limited electronic conductivity, insufficient capacity arising from incomplete redox utilization, and structural instability during cycling. Herein, we propose a synergistic engineering strategy integrated with conductive carbon coating to address these challenges. A multi-component NASICON cathode, Na3.25V1.44Fe0.25Mn0.25Mg0.02Nb0.02Zr0.02(PO4)3 (HE-NVP), is rationally designed, in which Fe³⁺ and Mn²⁺ substitution activates the reversible high-voltage V⁴⁺/V⁵⁺ redox couple, while Mg²⁺, Nb⁵⁺, and Zr⁴⁺ server as structural stabilizers to reinforce lattice integrity. The resulting configurational entropy and multi-element simultaneously regulate electronic structure, accelerate Na⁺ diffusion kinetics, and suppress structural degradation. Benefiting from these cooperative effects, HE-NVP delivers a high reversible specific capacity of 120.9 mAh g-1 at 1 C with an average voltage of 3.43 V. Remarkably, it maintains 82.4 mAh g-1 after 1100 cycles at 20 C, demonstrating excellent rate capability and long-term durability. In-situ X-ray diffraction reveals that Na⁺ storage proceeds via a highly reversible hybrid mechanism involving both solid-solution and two-phase reactions, underscoring the structural resilience of the entropy-stabilized framework. This study elucidates the mechanistic role of high-entropy design in unlocking high-voltage redox activity while mitigating phase instability, offering a viable materials engineering paradigm for advanced NASICON-type sodium-ion battery cathodes.
